newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reinsurance Australia targets premium rise.
newsitem.headline: Reinsurance Australia targets premium rise.

text.p: Reinsurance Australia Corp Ltd said on Thursday it expected to achieve modest premium growth in calendar 1997.

Chairman Peter Cadwallader told the annual general meeting that in spite of premium rate reductions and a stronger Australian dollar, there were many opportunities in world markets to generate new business at reasonable rates.
"As a result, we believe we can source sufficient new business to achieve modest premium growth in 1997," he said.
Cadwallader said Reinsurance Australia was not immune to rate reductions in world markets and had declined to renew about A$60 million of business which did not meet its premium rating requirement.
"Premium growth has also been restricted by the strengthening of the Australian dollar which has reduced premium income by five percent," Cadwallader said.
However, he said the diversification and geographic spread of the company's business tended to minimise the overall impact of these factors.
Gross written premium in calendar 1996 was A$527.3 million.
Reinsurance Australia said in February that it was targetting gross underwritten premium growth of 15 percent in 1997
The company reported a 31 percent rise in net profit to A$66.6 million for calendar 1996.
